children: Oracle
has invoked force majeure over potential delays at a major data center project developed by Blue Owl Capital
in New Mexico, putting fresh pressure on the financing model behind the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure.
The notice relates to Project Jupiter, a data center campus that Blue Owl Capital
's STACK Infrastructure is developing to support OpenAI
. The project is facing a delay of about one year because of difficulties securing power at the site, according to a
Reuters
report that cites a person familiar with Oracle's
notice and the deal.

The development is drawing increased attention from lenders and investors as financing for AI infrastructure expands at a rapid pace and questions grow around how construction, power, and other project risks are allocated.

"The financing side of the AI buildout is starting to ask much ​harder questions than the demand side," said Sean McDevitt, a partner at management consulting firm Arthur D. Little, according to the report. "The underlying demand still appears very strong, but investors and lenders are ​increasingly focused on how risk is allocated."
Blue Owl Capital
has about $3B of equity invested in Project Jupiter and earns a lower return while the facility is under construction, with returns increasing after completion. Oracle
invoked force majeure because of delays in securing power for the site, the person familiar with the matter said.
The delay means Blue Owl's
higher returns would begin later than originally expected. During the development stage, Blue Owl
earns a 9% yield on its equity, the separate report pointed out, adding that upon completion of the project, the levered yield is expected to be around 11%.
Despite the notice, Blue Owl said the parties remain committed to the project.
"Blue Owl, STACK Infrastructure and Oracle remain fully aligned on Project Jupiter. This notice does not change the financial commitments to this multiyear project," the company said.
The Jupiter situation comes as lenders and investors reassess the economics of large AI infrastructure projects, with higher U.S. interest rates and construction timelines drawing greater scrutiny.
Project Jupiter spans 1,400 acres and has secured $18B in loans from a consortium of banks. The project is part of Oracle's
broader effort to provide computing capacity for OpenAI
as AI demand drives an unprecedented expansion in data center construction.

title: Oracle-Blue Owl project delay puts spotlight on AI financing - report
